transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m… not really sure how to explain it. Lately when I’m walking across campus, it feels like I’m behind glass or something. Like I’m not quite in my own body, and the buildings and students around me don’t feel completely real. It scares me.
How long have you been feeling this way?
About six days. Since the lighting rig collapsed during the showcase.
Have you heard or seen anything that isn't there since the lighting rig collapsed?
No… I don’t think so. I haven’t heard voices or seen things, if that’s what you mean.
How have you been feeling emotionally since the lighting rig collapsed?
Mostly… numb, I guess. My husband tried to be sweet—cut flowers from the garden, made me tea—and I knew it was kind. I just couldn’t really feel anything good from it. Just kind of… heavy and blank.
Have you been feeling sad or depressed since the lighting rig collapsed?
I don’t know… sad, maybe, but mostly I just feel kind of shut down. It’s hard to sort out.
Have you been feeling anxious since the lighting rig collapsed?
I… I’m not sure. I feel on edge sometimes, but I don’t really know if that’s anxiety or just… everything feeling wrong.
Have you been avoiding any places or activities since the lighting rig collapsed?
Yeah… a bit. I’ve been going the long way around campus so I don’t have to pass the atrium. And if people bring up the showcase, I usually just… change the subject, or leave.
Do you feel like you're reliving the moment when the lighting rig collapsed?

Yeah… sometimes. Not like I’m fully back there, but the sound of it coming down just… barges in. I’ll be grading, or making coffee, and suddenly I can see him on the floor, and the students moving forward, like it’s right in front of me again.
Have you been trying to avoid thinking about the lighting rig collapsing?
Yeah… I think so. I try not to get into it. If someone mentions the showcase, I usually just change the subject or leave. And I’ve been taking the long way so I don’t have to pass the atrium.
Do you feel like you're observing yourself from outside your body at times?

Sometimes, yeah. It’s… hard to explain. When I’m walking across campus it feels like I’m watching everything through glass, like I’m not quite in my body. The buildings, the students… they seem a little unreal. It scares me.
Are there specific memories or thoughts about the lighting rig collapse that you've been trying to push away or not think about?

Yeah. I try not to let it get started. If someone brings up the showcase, I usually change the subject or just leave. And I’ve been going the long way around campus so I don’t have to pass the atrium.
Do you have any gaps in your memory about what happened when the lighting rig collapsed?
I… I’m not sure. I don’t think there are whole parts missing, exactly. It’s more just… blurry in places, but I can’t really tell.
Are there specific thoughts or feelings related to the lighting rig collapse that you've been trying to avoid thinking about?

Yeah… I mean, I try not to go there in my head. I’ve been taking the long way around so I don’t have to pass the atrium, and if someone mentions the showcase, I usually just change the subject or leave.
Are there any parts of what happened when the lighting rig collapsed that you just can't remember?
I don’t… I don’t think so. Not like a whole chunk is gone. Some of it feels kind of muddled, but I can’t point to a specific part I can’t remember.
Do you feel like you're disconnected from yourself or your surroundings most of the time?

Yeah… sometimes. Especially walking across campus. It feels like I’m sort of behind glass, like I’m there but not really in my body. Everything around me—the buildings, people—just feels a little unreal.
Has your daily life or relationships been significantly affected by these feelings of disconnection and numbness?

Yeah… it has. I haven’t really been doing my job the way I should. I walked out of a planning meeting, and I missed two mentoring sessions with students. I’ve also been avoiding parts of campus I’m supposed to use, so… it’s getting in the way.
Are there any specific things, such as people, places, or activities, that remind you of the lighting rig collapse and that you've been trying to avoid?
Yeah… the atrium, mostly. I’ve been taking the long way around campus so I don’t have to pass it. And if people bring up the showcase, I usually just… change the subject or leave.
Have you noticed any problems in your relationships with friends or family since the lighting rig collapsed?
A little, yeah. My husband’s been trying to be kind… he cut flowers from the garden and made me tea. I knew it was sweet, but I just couldn’t really feel it. It was just… blank, heavy.
